findings.defect: The CRE-R-24 plan's trigger path `POST /api/create/review/advance` is in no API mapping for TaskPublished (R-133e); the plan was withheld, so the committed manifest keeps only the skip row and the unmapped path survives solely in the job report.
findings.failureScenario: The plan is cached (D-82) and re-emitted unchanged on the next job once its Critical clause findings are fixed; the trigger is then sent to a `create` write path nothing in `API_MAP` confirms exists, so the test fails at the trigger (or hits a different route) and never exercises propagation, while the manifest row that would show the path is absent from the tree.
findings.evidence: R-133e (requirements.md:343 `(e) a \`trigger.path\` or read-back \`path\` that is not present in any configured API mapping (OQ-15).`); packages/core/src/api-map.ts:34-44 — `API_MAP` has keys `publisher`, `consumer`, `get-ready` only, and :42 `TaskPublished: { path: '/api/grdy/assignments/getTasks', ...}` is the sole TaskPublished path; adversarial-reports/1792676514926-j6neyt/report.json:154 `"defect": "The trigger POST /api/create/review/advance is in no API mapping for 'TaskPublished'."`; generated-tests/functional/manifest.json:101-102 `"requirement": "awp-app-plane/CRE-R-24", "reason": "adversarial: A-01, A-02, A-03, A-04, A-05, A-06"`; OQ-15 → (b), D-88 keeps this Major.

verification.reason: The R-133e violation itself is real: API_MAP has no `create` key and its only TaskPublished path is the get-ready read path, and the job report records the plan's trigger as POST /api/create/review/advance. The failure scenario cannot be traced to its end, though: the plan is withheld, so no committed file or manifest plan row carries the path; a cache hit reuses the identical plan (functest generate.ts:128-131) and validatePlan does not check clauses, so the plan is re-withheld for A-01…A-06 rather than 'fixed', and a re-synthesised plan may use a different path. The live create route table is not in the repo.

findings.defect: The functional emitter renders env-var names with dot access (`process.env.${pub.baseUrlEnv}`), and the conventional stem for an unmapped source (`envStem`) only guarantees `[A-Z0-9_]`, not a valid identifier, so a source label starting with a digit yields a syntactically invalid test file.
findings.failureScenario: ENTITY_FLOWS gains a flow whose publisher is a domain labelled `3rd-party` (unmapped, OQ-15): `envStem('3rd-party')` → `3RD_PARTY`, and the emitted file contains `const publisherBase = process.env.3RD_PARTY_API_URL;`, which is a SyntaxError — Vitest fails to load the file, so the suite errors rather than skipping (R-83a/D-26 'never fails without live creds' is broken) and R-134/R-133d regexes over the file text no longer match the shape they expect. The §3.9 emitter uses bracket access (`process.env["..."]`) and is not affected.
findings.evidence: packages/functest/src/emit.ts:108 `const publisherBase = process.env.${pub.baseUrlEnv};` :109-111 same for the other three; packages/functest/src/plan.ts:323-325 `export function envStem(source: string): string { return source.toUpperCase().replace(/[^A-Z0-9]+/g, '_'); }` :346 `{ role, source, baseUrlEnv: \`${envStem(source)}_API_URL\`, tokenEnv: \`${envStem(source)}_TOKEN\`, recordsAt: '', mapped: false }`; contrast packages/testgen/src/emit.ts:24 `const baseUrl = process.env[${JSON.stringify(t.target.baseUrlEnv)}];`

verification.reason: The emitter interpolates the env name after `process.env.` (dot access) on all four lines, and `envStem` only upper-cases and replaces non-[A-Z0-9] runs with `_`, so a source label beginning with a digit yields e.g. `process.env.3RD_PARTY_API_URL`, which is not a valid JavaScript member expression (identifiers cannot start with a digit) and makes the emitted file fail to parse instead of skipping. No guard exists: source labels are the ODCS `domain` string (metadata.ts:52, unsanitised), stampPlan applies envStem to any unmapped source, and validatePlan only checks that the source is in the grounded set. The trigger requires a digit-leading domain declared in ENTITY_FLOWS, which no current flow has, so the defect holds with a narrow trigger. The §3.9 emitter is unaffected because it uses bracket access.
verification.evidence: packages/functest/src/emit.ts:108 `const publisherBase = process.env.${pub.baseUrlEnv};`; packages/functest/src/plan.ts:323-325 `export function envStem(source: string): string { return source.toUpperCase().replace(/[^A-Z0-9]+/g, '_'); }` :346 `: { role, source, baseUrlEnv: \`${envStem(source)}_API_URL\`, tokenEnv: \`${envStem(source)}_TOKEN\`, recordsAt: '', mapped: false };`; packages/core/src/metadata.ts:52 `domain: str(doc.domain),`; contrast packages/testgen/src/emit.ts:24 `const baseUrl = process.env[${JSON.stringify(t.target.baseUrlEnv)}];`

findings.defect: `KNOWN_FORMATS` is a strict subset of what `ajv-formats` registers, so a contract `logicalTypeOptions.format` that Ajv could enforce (`url`, `uri-template`, `json-pointer`, `relative-json-pointer`, `iso-date-time`, `iso-time`, `int32`, `int64`, `float`, `double`, `byte`, `binary`, `password`) is silently dropped from the derived conformance schema.
findings.failureScenario: A get-ready property `resultsPackageLocation: { logicalType: string, logicalTypeOptions: { format: url } }` is added to the TaskPublished projection; deriveConstraints drops `format`, the embedded schema says only `type: string`, and a live record carrying `resultsPackageLocation: "not a url"` passes the conformance test although it violates a declared, Ajv-enforceable constraint (R-83c: 'each property's logicalTypeOptions that Ajv can enforce').
findings.evidence: packages/testgen/src/derive-schema.ts:62 `const KNOWN_FORMATS = new Set(['date', 'time', 'date-time', 'duration', 'uri', 'uri-reference', 'email', 'hostname', 'ipv4', 'ipv6', 'uuid', 'regex']);` :76 `if (typeof o.format === 'string' && KNOWN_FORMATS.has(o.format)) out.format = o.format;`; node_modules/ajv-formats/dist/formats.js:20 `"uri-template": /^(?:...)*$/i,` :23 `url: /^(?:https?|ftp):\/\/...` :34 `"json-pointer": /^(?:\/(?:[^~/]|~0|~1)*)*$/,` :42 `int32: { type: "number", validate: validateInt32 },` :14 `"iso-date-time": fmtDef(getDateTime(), compareIsoDateTime),`; R-83c (requirements.md:163 `format (only formats ajv-formats registers, e.g. uuid, date-time)`).

verification.reason: Traced end to end: `deriveConstraints` copies `format` only when it is in KNOWN_FORMATS (12 names), while the emitted conformance test calls `addFormats(new Ajv({ allErrors: true }))` with no options, which registers every name in ajv-formats' `formatNames` (index.js:8-15), and `fullFormats` includes `url`, `uri-template`, `json-pointer`, `relative-json-pointer`, `iso-time`, `iso-date-time`, `int32`, `int64`, `float`, `double`, `byte` (formats.js:13-14, 20, 23, 34, 37, 40-48). A contract `format: url` is therefore dropped although Ajv would have compiled and enforced it, and a record with a non-URL string passes the embedded schema's bare `type: string`. No live contract in the tree uses one of these formats, so the trigger is narrow.
verification.evidence: packages/testgen/src/derive-schema.ts:62 `const KNOWN_FORMATS = new Set(['date', 'time', 'date-time', 'duration', 'uri', 'uri-reference', 'email', 'hostname', 'ipv4', 'ipv6', 'uuid', 'regex']);` :76 `if (typeof o.format === 'string' && KNOWN_FORMATS.has(o.format)) out.format = o.format;`; generated-tests/conformance/get-ready.TaskPublished.generated.test.ts:80 `const validate = addFormats(new Ajv({ allErrors: true })).compile(schema);`; node_modules/ajv-formats/dist/index.js:14 `const list = opts.formats || formats_1.formatNames;` :31-32 `for (const f of list) ajv.addFormat(f, fs[f]);`; node_modules/ajv-formats/dist/formats.js:23 `url: /^(?:https?|ftp):\/\/...` :34 `"json-pointer": /^(?:\/(?:[^~/]|~0|~1)*)*$/,` :42 `int32: { type: "number", validate: validateInt32 },`

findings.defect: When one source carries two valid contracts whose `schema[0].name` is the same entity, the compat variant is picked by catalog input order (`variants.find(...)`) and both contracts receive the same conformance file path, so the output depends on input order and one emitted file silently overwrites the other.
findings.failureScenario: Catalog: `get-ready/urn:bawp:get-ready:assignments-api` and a second get-ready contract `urn:bawp:get-ready:tasks-feed` both with `schema[0].name: TaskPublished`. generate.ts:52-61 pushes two conformance entries; :115 renders both to `conformance/get-ready.TaskPublished.generated.test.ts`; scripts/generate-tests.ts:131-135 writes the second over the first, so the manifest lists two tests but the tree holds one, and the compat consumer at :79 is whichever contract the read API returned first — a re-crawl that reorders items changes the committed compat test with no catalog change (R-88).
findings.evidence: packages/testgen/src/generate.ts:78 `const pub = variants.find((v) => v.source === roles.publisher)!;` :79 `const con = variants.find((v) => v.source === roles.consumer)!;` :115 `? { path: \`conformance/${t.source}.${t.entity}.generated.test.ts\`, contents: emitConformanceTest(t, i) }`; scripts/generate-tests.ts:131-135 `for (const f of artifacts.files) { const full = join(destDir, f.path); ... writeFileSync(full, f.contents);`; R-88 (requirements.md:188); R-92 layout `conformance/<source>.<entity>.generated.test.ts` (requirements.md:189). Same pattern in packages/functest/src/ground.ts:148 `const canonical = variants.find((c) => c.source === roles.publisher)!;`.

verification.reason: Traced end to end: the entity is `schema[0].name` with no same-source uniqueness (metadata.ts:30-40); the conformance loop runs once per catalog contract and the file path is built from `${t.source}.${t.entity}` only, so two valid same-source contracts naming the same entity produce two manifest entries and one path, and the CLI's write loop writes both to that path in sequence (last wins). The compat variant choice at :78-79 is `variants.find(...)` over the unsorted catalog filter, so it follows input order. No dedupe exists in scripts/generate-tests.ts:91-109 or generate.ts:38-62; the only duplicate handling in packages/functions/src concerns requirement/contract ids (refresh.ts:7, :163). The trigger is absent from today's catalog (every source/entity pair in generated-tests/manifest.json is unique), so the severity 'narrow trigger' is right.
verification.evidence: packages/testgen/src/generate.ts:115 `? { path: \`conformance/${t.source}.${t.entity}.generated.test.ts\`, contents: emitConformanceTest(t, i) }`; :67 `const variants = catalog.filter((c) => c.entity === entity);` :78 `const pub = variants.find((v) => v.source === roles.publisher)!;`; scripts/generate-tests.ts:131-134 `for (const f of artifacts.files) { const full = join(destDir, f.path); mkdirSync(dirname(full), { recursive: true }); writeFileSync(full, f.contents);`; packages/core/src/metadata.ts:34-35 `const name = str(first?.name); if (name) return name;`

needsDecision.item: git status shows 7 generated files modified, but the content diff is empty (line endings only)
needsDecision.detail: `git diff --numstat -- generated-tests` printed nothing (no changed lines), while git status lists manifest.json, functional/manifest.json, the four compat files and the conformance file as modified; the only warnings were `LF will be replaced by CRLF`. The regenerated tree is therefore content-identical to HEAD (R-88 no-op holds on bytes the generator writes), but the repo has no .gitattributes pinning eol, so every regeneration on Windows shows as a full-tree change. Decide whether line-ending churn counts as an R-88 violation for the committed artifacts.

needsDecision.item: Disagree with critic findings C-19, C-15 and C-08: they describe spec-mandated behaviour as defects
needsDecision.detail: C-19 says `recordsOf` returning `[]` for an unrecognised envelope masks a malformed read-back; R-117b's last bullet and R-83 prescribe exactly this (record in body, `result.data`, or `result.data.json`; anything else is 'not found' and the test fails, not passes). C-15 and C-08 say `typeMatches(..., true)` / `exists` on `standards` pass on null; R-117b says `matchesType` and `exists` accept null precisely where the asserting contract marks the field nullable, and the get-ready contract marks `standards`, `description`, `duration` nullable. These three are Minor/Major critic items, report-only, and should not be read as defects of the emitter.
needsDecision.evidence: requirements.md:270 `the read-back SHALL find its record in the body, or in a tRPC envelope (\`result.data\`, \`result.data.json\`), when the mapped \`recordsAt\` is empty.`; requirements.md:268 `\`exists\` SHALL fail on \`null\` unless the asserting service's contract marks the field nullable`; requirements.md:264 `accepts null only where the asserting service's contract marks the field nullable (\`customProperties nullable="true"\`)`; packages/adversary/tests/__fixtures__/calibration/live-20261009/get-ready.assignments-api.odcs.yaml:114-119 `- name: standards ... customProperties: - property: nullable value: "true"`
